entities.summary:
Zacharias of Mytilene, known also as Zacharias Scholasticus or Zacharias Rhetor (c. 465 – after 536 CE), was a pivotal ecclesiastical historian, philosopher, and bishop whose writings offer invaluable insights into the intellectual and religious landscape of the late 5th and early 6th centuries. Born in Gaza, he pursued legal studies in Alexandria and Constantinople, immersing himself in both Neoplatonic philosophy and Christian theology. His career culminated in his appointment as Bishop of Mytilene on Lesbos, placing him at the intersection of imperial power and ecclesiastical authority during a period of intense theological ferment.

His most significant contribution is the 'Ecclesiastical History', a chronicle originally spanning 450 to 491 CE, although only an abridged Syriac version survives. This work details the complex religious politics of the Byzantine Empire, including the aftermath of the Council of Chalcedon and the rise of Miaphysitism. Beyond history, Zacharias engaged deeply with philosophical debates, notably in his dialogue 'Ammonius', which critiques Neoplatonism from a Christian perspective, and his 'Disputation with the Manichaean', demonstrating his commitment to orthodox Christian doctrine against perceived heresies. His 'Life of Severus of Antioch' further illustrates his engagement with prominent theological figures of his era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Zacharias Rhetor's 'Ecclesiastical History' is an indispensable primary source for the religious and political history of the late 5th-century Byzantine Empire, offering unique insights into the Chalcedonian controversies and early Miaphysitism. His philosophical works also exemplify the crucial intellectual transition from classical thought to Christian scholasticism.
